answer: An applicant escrows a pearl bond equal to one epoch of median revenue and publishes a pigment: the hash of a TPM-signed execution diary bound to one device key. Each epoch a random gale samples 8% of diaries, re-runs chosen intervals, and matches the pigment on-chain. A reused pigment or divergent diary slashes the entire pearl and blacklists that device key for 30 epochs. The bond vests only after four consecutive clean samples, so N identities cost N devices plus N locked pearls.
